sections.overview: This fossorial rodent inhabits eastern European steppe and forest-steppe, with strong populations in eastern Ukraine extending east toward the Volga.
sections.identification: Its eyes are reduced and covered by skin; powerful incisors and a reduced tail are adaptations associated with underground life.
sections.habitat: In eastern Ukraine it is associated with preserved steppe, meadow-steppe and open slopes of ravines.
sections.diet: It eats underground plant parts and may store roots and other food in burrow chambers.
sections.behavior: It excavates long, shallow feeding tunnels and deeper chambers; juveniles may appear above ground while dispersing.
sections.reproduction: A field study in the Velikoburlutskyi Steppe reported one annual litter of one to three pups.
sections.ecology: Its eastern Ukrainian distribution is uneven, and field studies associate it with remaining steppe patches; cultivation and fragmentation are reported pressures on steppe fauna.
sections.conservation: The Ukrainian museum species page assigns no conservation category; local habitat pressures should not be mistaken for a global assessment.
